**Bots can place and click CraftEngine furniture, and a busy server no longer floods the event record.**

Existing scenarios run with the same arguments and get answers of the same shape. Three things answer differently: a bot click now turns the bot to its target first, `drop_item` presses the drop key instead of throwing the stack out of the inventory screen, and a command whose handler throws now comes back as `dispatched: false` instead of failing the call. The event and command fixes are in the server plugin, so they need the 3.2.3 agent on the server.

### Fixed

**Bots place and click CraftEngine furniture.** On Purpur 1.21.8 with CraftEngine 26.9, a bot could neither place furniture nor click it, while `PlayerInteractEvent` still fired uncancelled.
- `use_block` clicked the centre of the block, so ground furniture stood half inside the block it was placed on and CraftEngine's obstruction check refused it. The click now lands on the middle of the named face, after the bot has turned to it.
- `use_entity` picked the nearest entity, which for furniture is the `item_display` it is drawn with; the server only logged `PlayerUseUnknownEntityEvent`. `use_entity` and `attack_entity` now skip entities a client cannot pick, turn to the target and wait for the turn to reach the server, then send the real hit point and sneak state. The reply keeps the entity id and adds which entity it was and how far away.
- `drop_item` presses the drop key the way a player presses Q. It reports whether the item came out or the server handed it back.

**Microsoft sign-in is refused on a runner too old to do it.** A runner from before 3.1.1 ignored `auth: microsoft`, so the bot joined offline under the account's name and an online-mode server kicked it with `unverified_username`. The runner now reports its release; `bot_spawn` refuses `auth: microsoft` on a runner that reports none, and refuses an auth it does not know. `session_start` shows `runnerVersion`, and `runnerWarning` when the runner is not this server's release.

**One flooding event type no longer evicts the rest.** On a proxied server, `HopperInventorySearchEvent` fired hundreds of times a second with nobody online, the event buffer turned over in minutes, and the event being looked for was gone. It joins the high-frequency list. As a backstop, any event type with no player involved is capped per second: past `event-rate-limit` (200 by default, 0 turns it off) the rest of that second is counted, not kept. Events involving a player, and the types in `reinstate-types`, are never capped. `events_summary` lists capped types under `rateLimited`, and `server_info` shows the limit and the total.

**A command that throws is reported, not failed.** When a command's handler threw, `command_exec` let it escape: the caller got a bare internal error and the console logged `Error handling tools/call`, which read like a fault in the agent. It now answers `dispatched: false` with the root cause, a note that whatever ran before the throw has already happened, and the hash `exceptions_recent` opens the stack with.

**Inventory queries read custom model data again.** On 1.21.4 and later, every inventory query reported no model data for items that carry it, because the getter was looked up on Paper's package-private item meta class. It is now read through the public API types.

### Upgrading

Install as before. Update the server plugin to 3.2.3 to get the event cap, the command report and the model-data fix; the bot fixes and the runner check work with the 3.2.0–3.2.2 agent too. If you point `runnerJar` at a runner of your own, use this release's, or leave it out and let the server pick the bundled one.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Backas03/VitaminMCP/compare/3.2.2...3.2.3
